Queens By Linkedin
Crown Each Region
![crossclimb](https://images.forbes.com/fbs-games-assets/crossclimb.png)
Crossclimb By Linkedin
Unlock A Trivia Ladder
Sony typically reveals the upcoming PS Plus Essential lineup on the last Wednesday of the month and releases the new games on the first Tuesday of the coming month. That’s not always the case, but it’s a good rule of thumb.
This means that September's PS Plus Essential games get announced August 26 and go live September 1, with Extra and Premium’s first wave revealed September 9 and dropping on September 15.
This means there’s only a six-day gap between the reveal and the drop, because September 1 is itself the first Tuesday of the month. It also means August's Dying Light 2, Big Walk, and Signalis — all very much worth downloading if you’re a PS Plus subscriber — expire August 31. Don’t sleep on these games!
PS Plus September 2026 Games Leaked
Update: The September lineup of PS Plus games just leaked online, a day before the official announcement. The leak comes by way off billbil-kun at Dealabs, who has accurately leaked countless PS Plus lineups prior to their official reveal. The games for September reportedly include Sniper Elite: Resistance, Chained Echoes, and Wobbly Life. None of these were in my own predictions, unfortunately. Billbil-kun has an exceptionally strong track record with PlayStation Plus leaks, accurately revealing monthly games ahead of Sony’s official announcements for years. While no leak should be treated as official confirmation, his PS Plus reports have historically been highly reliable. We’ll know for sure when Sony reveals the lineup officially.
- Sniper Elite: Resistance has a Mostly Positive user review score on Steam. It’s a third-person stealth-and-snipe shooter that takes place in WWII France during the Nazi occupation.
- Chained Echoes is a 16-bit style JRPG set in a fantasy world “where dragons are as common as piloted mechanical suits.” It’s a modern take on the turn-based NES classics of old and has a Very Positive user review score on Steam.
- Wobbly Life rounds out these wildly different titles and gives you something to play with friends. The co-op game is all about playing together in vibrant sandbox worlds, building stuff and solving puzzles, playing mini-games and upgrade your vehicles and houses. It has an Overwhelmingly Positive user review score on Steam.
The games will release on Tuesday, September 1. Be sure to download August’s free PS Plus Essential lineup before it’s too late!
[Original Story]
So far there have been no reliable leaks for September's PS Plus lineup. If one arrives, it'll almost certainly come from billbil-kun at Dealabs, who has been the most accurate PS Plus leaker going for years now and who typically posts the month's headline title anywhere from one to seven days before Sony's reveal. That gives us a narrow window: the official announcement is expected Wednesday, August 26, though Sony jumped a day early last month so it’s always possible the reveal could come sooner.
We can also look at what’s coming out to see if we can glean any clues, but here again we come up mostly dry. No video games appear to be releasing on September 1, but Trine 6 comes out on September 17 and I’ve had Trine 5 on my wishlist for sometime now. That’s something!
If we look back at previous years, past September releases are also very little help.
Previous September PS Plus Essential Lineups
Looking back at the PS Plus September lineup over the last seven years, it’s hard to really come up with any coherent theme. Here’s what we’ve gotten since 2019:
2019 — Batman: Arkham Knight, Darksiders III
2020 — PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds, Street Fighter V
2021 — Overcooked! All You Can Eat, Predator: Hunting Grounds, Hitman 2
2022 — Granblue Fantasy: Versus, Need For Speed Heat, Toem
2023 — Saints Row (2022), Black Desert Traveler Edition, Generation Zero
2024 — Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions, MLB The Show 24, Little Nightmares II
2025 — Psychonauts 2, Stardew Valley, Viewfinder
Basically, there’s no telling what September will bring. Sometimes we get horror games (a little early for Halloween) and the occasional sports title. Some indie stuff. A couple of racing games. It’s really an anything goes!
A raft of PS Plus Extra games (and a couple Premium) titles will leave the service in mid-September, including: Persona 5 Tactica, Shadowrun Returns, Shadowrun Hong Kong: Extended Edition, Shadowrun Dragonfall: Director's Cut, Romance of the Three Kingdoms XIII, Toukiden 2, Bubsy: The Woolies Strike Back, EA Sports Madden NFL 26, and — on Premium — Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue and Toy Story 3.
It’s unlikely that any of these will come to Essential the same month they leave Extra or Premium, but we could get something to fill the void — a JRPG perhaps.
My 3 Predictions For September PS Plus
Spider-Man 2 — The headliner for September riding on the coattails of the massive success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day. It’s a popular game and there’s no better time than striking while the iron is hot. Besides, the new Wolverine game comes out in September, so this would be a pleasant pairing.
Trine 5 — The indie title of the list. The little guy, but a great fun co-op fantasy game you can play with friends. Might be too soon to the next game’s release, however. But I want an indie title in my predictions trio and this is what I’m going with!
Stellar Blade — Shift Up is working on the sequel, Blood Rain, and there’s no better way to drive a little hype than with a free PS Plus release of the original action game. Of course, the sequel is still a long ways out, but Stellar Blade has been out long enough to make sense on PS Plus regardless.
Now, onto the wishlist!
PS Plus September 2026 PS Plus Wishlist
Some of these are more likely candidates than others and some of these are quite obviously just wishful thinking. Most of these remain from past prediction lists, since they haven’t been picked yet!
Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered — This is a modern classic open-world adventure game about fighting giant robotic dinosaurs in a post-apocalyptic future. It seems like the perfect candidate for a PS Plus title, since the remaster came out two years ago.
Atomfall — The first-person survival-action game set in an alternate-history 1960s Britain after a nuclear disaster is a top pick for a lot PS Plus hopefuls. It only released in early 2025, however, so it’s pretty new for a PS Plus inclusion. Then again, we’ve seen quicker turnarounds (Dragon Age: The Veilguard for instance).
Fallout 4: Anniversary Edition — Two reasons for this. One, there’s an Anniversary Edition out and the second season of Amazon’s excellent Fallout series has renewed interest in the series.
Dispatch — An absolutely wonderful interactive movie style superhero game that blends gorgeous animation and incredible writing and acting with a fun superhero management sim.
Kingdom Come: Deliverance — The excellent Medieval RPG is many years old now, and the sequel just came out. Why not release the original on PS Plus? Well...I guess because it was a PS4-era game. But they could release the sequel!
Blue Prince — One of my favorite games of 2025, this would make a great indie title to go with some bigger releases. What an absolute gem.
Resident Evil 4 Remake — The remake of the popular action-horror game from 2005 was released in 2023 to wide acclaim. It’s old enough to be a contender for a PS Plus release and would definitely be a crowd-pleaser.
Elden Ring — FromSoftware’s mega-hit action-RPG would be a huge win for Sony and PlayStation Plus gamers. Even Demon’s Souls Remake would be a massive win, though I put both of these in the “wishful thinking” column. Still, Elden Ring might make sense given the recent release of the standalone multiplayer spinoff Nightreign.
Star Wars Outlaws — Ubisoft’s open-world Star Wars game wasn’t the hit they needed, but it’s still a pretty fun way to head to a galaxy far, far away and rub shoulders with scum and villainy. It would make a really perfect PS Plus release.
Death Stranding — Hideo Kojima’s weirdest game was a big enough hit to commission a sequel and that sequel just came out in 2025. Makes sense to get the original onto PS Plus at some point, if only to drive more people to the newer (and more expensive) sequel.
Street Fighter 6 — The popular fighting game franchise continues to be a crowd-pleaser, and releasing this 2023 game on PS Plus would be fun despite getting a fighting game last month. That makes me doubtful we’ll see this one, but I’d play it if Sony put it out there.
Squirrel with a Gun — As the title indicates, this is a little game where you play as a squirrel with a gun. It’s the kind of indie title that often accompanies bigger, AAA releases in a PS Plus lineup.
Assassin’s Creed Mirage — Releasing a free Assassin’s Creed game makes sense with the Black Flag remake on the horizon. Get people excited about the re-release. It’s already been added to Extra and Premium, of course.
(Prediction Now!) Trine 5 — I used to absolutely love the Trine games. I remember playing them with my kids when they were little. The gorgeous artwork in those games plus the couch co-op just made them such a delight. Then I forgot about them, and I actually never did play the fifth game. I’d love to, though. It would be super nostalgic for the whole family. Here’s hoping!
All The PS Plus Essential Games Released In 2026
Here’s what we’ve nabbed so far.
January 2026
- Need for Speed Unbound
- Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed
- Core Keeper
February 2026
- Undisputed
- Subnautica: Below Zero
- Ultros
- Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown
March 2026
- PGA Tour 2K25
- Monster Hunter Rise
- Slime Rancher 2
- The Elder Scrolls Online: Gold Road Collection
April 2026
- Lords of the Fallen
- Tomb Raider 1-3 Remastered
- Sword Art Online: Fractured Daydream
May 2026
- EA Sports FC 26
- Nine Sols
- Wuchang: Fallen Feathers
June 2026
- Grounded: Fully Yoked Edition
- Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl 2
- Warhammer 40,000: Darktide
July 2026
- Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III
- For the King II
- CrossCode
August 2026
- Dying Light 2 Stay Human: Reloaded Edition (PS4, PS5)
- Big Walk (PS5, day one)
- Signalis (PS4)
PS Plus Current Pricing
US PlayStation Plus pricing as of now:
- Essential — $10.99/month, $27.99/quarter, $79.99/year
- Extra — $16.99/month, $43.99/quarter, $134.99/year
- Premium — $19.99/month, $54.99/quarter, $159.99/year
PS Plus pricing went up earlier this year. Sony announced the increase on May 18, 2026, effective for new customers from May 20 — Essential, Extra and Premium climbed to $10.99, $16.99 and $19.99 monthly, with the three-month options rising to $27.99, $43.99 and $54.99.
Interestingly, annual plans were not raised, holding at $79.99, $134.99 and $159.99, and remain at their pre-hike rates as of August 2026. This is a departure from the September 2023 price hike, which jacked up both annual and monthly prices at the same time.
What games would you like to see come to PS Plus this September? Any insights or predictions? Any leaks I should know about? Let me know on Twitter or Facebook. Also be sure to subscribe to my YouTube channel and follow me here on this blog. You can also sign up for my Substack newsletter, Diabolical, where I talk culture and politics and the arts.
summary: Ahead of Sony's official announcement, the September 2026 PS Plus Essential games reportedly leaked online via reliable insider billbil-kun. The leaked lineup features Sniper Elite: Resistance, Chained Echoes, and Wobbly Life. Subscribers have until August 31 to claim August's current free games, including Dying Light 2 and Big Walk, before the new titles release on September 1.
key_points: September 2026 PS Plus Essential games reportedly leaked as Sniper Elite: Resistance, Chained Echoes, and Wobbly Life.
August's PS Plus games (Dying Light 2, Signalis, and Big Walk) expire on August 31.
The new Essential games are scheduled to go live on Tuesday, September 1.
Several titles are scheduled to leave the PS Plus Extra and Premium tiers in mid-September.

title: City Builder LEGO Skylines Announced for PS5, and It Seems Like a Perfect Match
author: Push Square; Stephen Tailby
content:
![City Builder LEGO Skylines Announced for PS5, and It Seems Like a Perfect Match 1](https://images.pushsquare.com/9f781b24a3af8/city-builder-lego-skylines-announced-for-ps5-and-it-seems-like-a-perfect-match-1.900x.jpg)
Publisher Paradox Interactive has just announced LEGO Skylines, and it's confirmed for PS5.
This is a city building sim from the development team currently also working on Cities: Skylines 2, which has yet to make its way to Sony's console.
Take a look at the announcement trailer here:
If you ask me, a LEGO city builder seems like the perfect fit of genre and licence.
![YouTube Video](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/y-XGB8_bQ3s/maxresdefault.jpg) Watch on
Subscribe to Push Square on YouTube171k
Going by the official description on the game's PS Store page, it sounds quite freeform — or at least, it'll give you lots of options to build out your city how you want to.
Cover the basics like electricity, food, and water. Then make it a place your citizens will love. Give them homes that one-up the neighbors. Good jobs. Great parks. Donut shops on every corner because that would be awesome. A frankly absurd amount of buildings, decorations, and other cool stuff (customization stuff) will make it easy to create a city that’s got your fingerprints all over it.
LEGO Skylines puts you in charge of, well, everything. Remember hospitals to keep everyone in one piece. Wheat for the donuts. Garbage collection, sewage, and all the other things that make a city click. How it all comes together is up to you. So stick your hard hat on and greenlight your weirdest ideas. Tweak one thing more times than you'd admit. And let yourself enjoy a little just-for-fun fun. It’s about the satisfaction of putting everything just where you want it. Which is, of course, exactly where it belongs.
There's no release date attached to this one yet — hopefully it's not too far off.
Are you interested in LEGO Skylines? Tell us in the comments section below.
[source youtube.com]
summary: Publisher Paradox Interactive has announced LEGO Skylines, a new city-building simulation game confirmed for the PS5. Developed by the same team working on Cities: Skylines 2, the game offers freeform building with extensive customization options. Players will manage essential city services like utilities, jobs, and healthcare while designing their ideal LEGO city.
key_points: LEGO Skylines has been announced by publisher Paradox Interactive for the PS5.
The game is developed by the same team currently working on Cities: Skylines 2.
Players must manage city basics such as electricity, food, water, garbage collection, and sewage.
The game features a wide variety of buildings, decorations, and customization options with no release date announced yet.

title: NBA 2K27 Is Teasing a GTA 6-Themed Event in Collaboration with Rockstar Games
author: Cade Onder
content:
NBA 2K27 is teasing a crossover with Rockstar Games, seemingly to promote Grand Theft Auto 6.
At the end of the trailer for NBA 2K27 Season 1, there's a very cryptic tease. The camera tilts down toward a purple-ish poster sporting palm trees, which looks awfully similar to the very first artwork Rockstar released for GTA 6. Seagulls and police sirens can be heard in the background before the camera pans over to an arcade cabinet. One machine has the 2K logo and the other has the Rockstar Games logo. On the screens, the words "Season 3" can be seen in the GTA 6 font and color scheme.
Seasons tend to last about six weeks, so we can expect Season 3 to launch around the time of GTA 6's release in November. It's unclear what exactly this will offer, especially since NBA 2K is an E-rated game and the GTA series pushes the boundaries with its M-ratings. However, it appears to be part of a larger effort to ramp up marketing for what will undoubtedly be one of the biggest releases in entertainment history.
A lot of fans have been frustrated with the lack of marketing for GTA 6 up until now. There have been two trailers and some screenshots to go along with pre-orders, but that's about it as of right now. However, things will ramp up later this week when Rockstar Games releases an extended look at the game on Netflix. Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick previously teased a big marketing campaign for GTA 6, and it seems like the decision to partner with Netflix and Take-Two's other juggernaut franchise, NBA 2K, will help emphasize the significance of this release.
Maybe players will be able to rep Vice City-themed gear or maybe there will be a Vice City basketball court in NBA 2K27. Basketball appears to be a part of GTA 6, as recently revealed in leaked gameplay for the title, but it's unclear how big of a role that mini-game will play in GTA 6. Either way, all will be revealed in the coming months.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.
summary: NBA 2K27 has teased a crossover with Rockstar Games to promote the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto 6. The trailer for NBA 2K27 Season 1 featured subtle references including a palm tree poster, audio cues, and arcade cabinets displaying "Season 3" in the GTA 6 font and color scheme. This collaboration is part of a broader marketing push for GTA 6, which also includes an upcoming extended look on Netflix.
key_points: NBA 2K27's Season 1 trailer included cryptic teases hinting at a Grand Theft Auto 6 crossover for Season 3.
The teaser featured palm tree visuals, police sirens, seagulls, and arcade cabinets with the Rockstar Games logo.
Season 3 is expected to launch around November, coinciding with the anticipated release of GTA 6.
Rockstar Games is also ramping up marketing by releasing an extended look at GTA 6 on Netflix.

title: WhatsApp announces three ways to make accounts more secure - 9to5Mac
author: Marcus Mendes
content:
![](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/08/whatsapp-security.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
Meta today announced a set of new security features for WhatsApp, including expanded passkey support and stronger two-step verification. Here are the details.
WhatsApp announces account security features
Meta today announced that WhatsApp now supports more than one passkey for the same account, a welcome feature for users who use both iOS and Android devices.
WhatsApp says more than 1 billion people now use passkeys to log back into their accounts with Face ID, Touch ID, or a screen lock code. The company first introduced passkey support on Android in October 2023 and expanded it to iPhone the following April.
Additionally, WhatsApp announced today that its two-step verification feature is expanding beyond a six-digit PIN to support full alphanumeric passwords, including special characters.
As WhatsApp explains, “two-step verification is an extra protection layer that helps prevent someone from taking over your account, even if they get hold of your one-time passcode,” and you can learn more about that here.
Finally, alas, this last feature is only available on Android for now, WhatsApp is adding a feature designed to make calls from unknown contacts safer to pick up.
From the press release:
When you get a call from someone not saved in your contacts, a little context can help you decide whether to pick up. On Android, you’ll now see more information about a non-contact caller, like whether the number is from a different country and if you have any groups in common. Scammers rely on urgency – now you can take a beat with some more info before answering.
It is worth mentioning that iPhone users can rely on a similar feature for traditional phone calls. Apple’s Call Screening feature, available on iPhones running iOS 26, automatically asks unknown callers for their name and reason for calling before the iPhone rings. Although it does not work with WhatsApp calls, you can learn more about it here.
To learn more about the security features WhatsApp announced today, follow this link.

title: Apple Unveils 2nm M6, Quad-Die M5 Ultra Chips with New Mac Mini and Mac Studio
author: Digital Foundry; William Judd
content:
![Apple Silicon M6 and M5 Ultra chips](https://images.digitalfoundry.net/3f41b2d89821a/apple-silicon-m6-and-m5-ultra-chips.970x.jpg)
Apple continues to set a blistering pace in adopting new processes for its Apple Silicon chips, with the Californian company today unveiling its first 2nm part, the M6, and its first quad-die chip, the M5 Ultra. The two new APUs are used in the latest generation of Mac computers, specifically the M6 Mac Mini and the M5 Ultra Mac Studio.
The M6 system-on-chip includes a 12-core CPU with two super cores, four performance cores and six efficiency cores, plus a 12-core GPU and dual 16-core Neural Engine. The M6 supports up to 170GB/s of memory bandwidth.
Meanwhile, the M5 Ultra is formed from two M5 Max chips, for a total of four dies joined via an "UltraFusion" interconnect. That allows for the APU to max out at 36 CPU cores (12 super, 24 performance) and 80 GPU cores with neural accelerators, with 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth. Apple is quoting a 25 percent gain in single-core performance, a 30 percent gain in multi-core performance and a 50 gain in memory bandwidth versus the M3 Ultra chip that arrived nearly 18 months ago.
![mac models compared m6 mac mini m5 ultra mac studio](https://images.digitalfoundry.net/eda828b339485/mac-models-compared-m6-mac-mini-m5-ultra-mac-studio.970x.jpg)
As you might guess, all of this comes at a steep cost, with the M6 Mac Mini starting at £899/$899 and the faster M5 Pro equipped model coming it at nearly double, £1,899/$1,699. The M6 model includes 16GB of memory by default, with 24GB costing an extra £200/$200 or 32GB costing an extra £400/$400. If you want to upgrade the 256GB of storage, you're looking at a £200/$200 premium for a 512GB drive, a £500/$500 premium for a 1TB size and a £1000/$1000 premium for a 2TB model.
That's pocket change compared to the Mac Studio, with the M5 Max model starting at £2,499/$2,499 and the top-end M5 Ultra chip starting at $5,499/£5,499. If you tick every option on the Mac Studio, you're looking at a 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU, 256GB of unified memory and 16TB of storage for just $18,299/£18,299.
Of course, while Apple is certainly charging a healthy premium for these upgrades, it is worth pointing out that prices have risen in the PC industry across the board due to the insane demand AI industries are putting on flash memory manufacturing, with SSDs and RAM being the most significantly affected components. Presumably, these prices take into account the supply situation in the future instead of right now, and things are only expected to get worse.
Still, it's interesting to see some new tech, and I'll be fascinated to see what the new Macs are capable of when it comes to gaming - even if local AI workloads and creative endeavours are very much the focus here.
summary: Apple has announced its first 2nm chip, the M6, and its first quad-die chip, the M5 Ultra, powering the latest Mac Mini and Mac Studio models. The M6 features a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, while the M5 Ultra combines four dies using an UltraFusion interconnect to offer up to 36 CPU cores and 80 GPU cores. These new computers come at a steep cost, with base prices starting at $899 for the Mac Mini and reaching up to $18,299 for a fully upgraded Mac Studio.
key_points: Apple unveiled its first 2nm chip (M6) and first quad-die chip (M5 Ultra).
The M6 chip powers the new Mac Mini, featuring a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, and dual 16-core Neural Engine.
The M5 Ultra powers the new Mac Studio, offering up to 36 CPU cores, 80 GPU cores, and 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth.
The M6 Mac Mini starts at $899, while the top-end M5 Ultra Mac Studio starts at $5,499 and can reach $18,299 fully upgraded.

title: Geralt Returns in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past and Remastered
author: Will Fulton; XBOX Wire Editor
content:
Over a decade ago, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt launched and cemented its place as one of the most acclaimed RPGs of the generation. Ever since, players have been discovering — and returning — to this dark fantasy world, immersing themselves in the lands of the Continent. And on September 29, they’ll have another way of experiencing Geralt of Rivia’s epic story with The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered on XBOX Series X|S!
Revealed on stage at gamescom Opening Night Live, Remastered will bring a wide range of improvements and modernizations to the game, upgrading the experience while maintaining the heart and soul of the original. And if you saw the announcement trailer, you also caught a glimpse of the upcoming Songs of the Past expansion, releasing in 2027. But we’ll get to that later! First, let’s talk about some of the key upgrades coming with Remastered.
![The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered screenshot](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/TW3RE_Gamescom_Boat_FIN_Xbox_16x9_CLEAN-2bf2cb8f899e07c6c8d9-1024x576.jpg)
Visually, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered aims to bring the game up to more modern, contemporary standards. You can see this not only through the improved textures across the environment — as well as NPC and monsters — but also the reworked lighting.
Throughout the open world, you’ll see more natural illumination and dramatically improved light and shadow. You’ll notice it in the foliage while hunting monsters in the wilderness, in the streets of Novigrad as the sun sets over the bustling market — all across the world. Together with improvements to ray tracing, these changes will make it feel like you’re seeing the world of The Witcher 3 for the first time again.
![The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered screenshot](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/TW3RE_Gamescom_City_Vista_FIN_Xbox_16x9_CLEAN-3ed3b091b7bedb43eb14-1024x576.jpg)
Of course, looks are one thing, but how does it feel? Modernization is also a key consideration here. Changes have been made to combat, traversal, and general movement too.
When it comes to combat, the action now feels more precise and smooth than ever before. Revamped animations play a decisive role here, with Geralt closing the gap in combat much more fluidly now, for example. Some brutal new finishers also enter the fray, including the Aard-based finisher that you can see in the trailer. The new adaptive camera also feeds into the way the action is presented; it’s more dynamic and lets you feel more immersed in the moment-to-moment swordfighting. Depending on how many foes you’re facing, the camera will now move in tighter or zoom out for a wider view of your enemies. The goal is to make this feel natural, smooth, and keep you engrossed and aware in battle at all times.
![The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered screenshot](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/TW3RE_Gamescom_Combat_Signs_FIN_Xbox_16x9_CLEAN-b10fc3ec754f546613d1-1024x576.jpg)
One of the biggest mechanical changes you’ll find in Remastered relates to skill trees and character progression. When looking at The Witcher 3 holistically, it became clear that there are ways to bring skill trees and character building more in-line with what a modern RPG audience might expect or be used to. Naturally, this is a pretty fundamental change. The entire system has been reimagined. New perks and abilities have been added, many existing skills have been reworked, and with the skill trees themselves completely redesigned, unlocking and creating your build becomes more flexible and intuitive.
There’s much, much more to talk about with the additions in Remastered, but for now let’s just quickly shout out a few more:
- Transmogrification — Reforge the look of your favorite weapons and armor through the magic of transmogrification! Now you never need to sacrifice style for stats. Geralt’s style is yours to command.
- Cross-platform mod support —  With mods available on XBOX Series X|S, you can create and play a wealth of custom content. From new quests, weapons, and equipment to balance changes and more, mods create an entirely unique Witcher 3 experience.
- Expanded photo mode — Make memories and capture thrilling moments with a wide array of photo mode options, including new poses, camera controls, frames, filters, models, and more.
And Remastered also supports XBOX Play Anywhere! Enjoy seamless play across your XBOX Series X|S, PC, or XBOX-supported handheld, and carry on your upgraded adventure without missing a beat.
![The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered screenshot](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/TW3RE_Gamescom_Combat_Group_FIN_Xbox_16x9_CLEAN-192dc78f6ae2ef7c0e1b-1024x576.jpg)
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered launches on September 29 as a free upgrade for all owners of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt on XBOX Series X|S. What’s more, players who only own the The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt base game will receive both Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine expansions for free. This includes players on XBOX One. Digital owners will automatically receive the expansions in their library, while disc-based players can claim the expansions for free from the Store.
Of course, Remastered is not the only time we saw Geralt appear at Opening Night Live. Geralt returns to the Path in the third expansion, Songs of the Past, coming in 2027. The trailer gave a small glimpse into the dark story that awaits players when they enter the brand-new realm of Letten — Dandelion’s homeland. Geralt travels alongside his good friend to support him in a personal matter, and together they find a land of peace and prosperity… Not the place for a witcher, right?
Well, in true CD PROJEKT RED storytelling fashion, there cannot be light without darkness. And in Letten, there is a darkness lurking beneath the surface; something that needs the expertise of a witcher. Something only Geralt can solve.
Songs of the Past also features never-before-seen monsters for Geralt to hunt down and face. To even the odds, the White Wolf will be equipped with new options in combat. New mutagens will be available in the expansion as well as a new weapon that some veteran The Witcher fans might recognize… That’s right, the chain! The chain weapon gives Geralt more variety in battle, especially when it comes to crowd control. The chain itself is a nod back to the intro cinematic for the original The Witcher game, and it is great to have it become a full-fledged part of the game here in Songs of the Past!
![The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered screenshot](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/W3SoP_Wood_Witch_FIN_PC_16x9_CLEAN-ed9700e70d34e8daae55-1024x576.jpg)
This expansion will launch in 2027. It is available to wishlist now on XBOX Series X|S, and benefits from all the upgrades included in Remastered, too! Stay tuned for more information on Geralt’s next adventure in Songs of the Past at a later date. We hope you’re ready to return to the Path!
summary: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered is launching on September 29 for Xbox Series X|S, bringing visual enhancements, improved combat mechanics, modernized skill trees, cross-platform mod support, and a photo mode. The remaster will be a free upgrade and includes the Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine expansions for base game owners. Additionally, a brand-new expansion titled Songs of the Past was announced for release in 2027, featuring a new story in Letten, fresh monsters, and the return of the chain weapon.
key_points: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered launches on September 29 for Xbox Series X|S with improved textures, reworked lighting, and ray tracing.
Combat and movement are updated with smoother animations, new finishers like an Aard-based attack, and a dynamic adaptive camera.
The character progression and skill tree systems have been entirely redesigned to fit modern RPG standards.
Remastered introduces cross-platform mod support, transmogrification, an expanded photo mode, and Xbox Play Anywhere compatibility.
A new expansion, Songs of the Past, is scheduled for release in 2027 and will feature a story in Dandelion's homeland of Letten along with new monsters and the chain weapon.

title: WhatsApp two-step verification codes are ditching six-digit PINs for full passwords
author: Ben Schoon
content:
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/08/whatsapp-security-updates.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
WhatsApp is making some security upgrades, including turning two-step verification codes into full passwords instead of the traditional six-digit numerical PIN.
Alongside celebrating that one billion of its users are now using passkeys, WhatsApp has two new account security features rolling out.
The first is an upgrade to two-step verification codes used with WhatsApp.
No longer are these codes just a six-digit numerical PIN, but a full password. WhatsApp says these will be “longer, alphanumeric,” and include special characters (@,$, etc) to make the password harder to guess. w
Two-step verification is getting stronger: Two-step verification is an extra protection layer that helps prevent someone from taking over your account, even if they get hold of your one-time passcode. Until now it was a six-digit PIN, we’ve now upgraded it to a full password: longer, alphanumeric, and even with special ch@racters to make it harder to guess. If you’ve been using “123456,” this is your sign to upgrade.
On Android, WhatsApp is also rolling out a new screen for calls that are coming from unknown callers, with the incoming call screen now showing context such as country of origin and whether or not the number is in any of the groups you’re in.

All in all, it seems like Xiaomi's self-developed chipset has really grown up and will be a serious competitor to the best that Qualcomm, MediaTek, and Apple have to offer.
